common_name: Flavor Supreme Pluot (Original Red-Fleshed Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; Flavor Supreme was one of the first Zaiger Genetics pluots introduced and remains one of the highest-flavored, with mottled maroon-and-green skin over vivid magenta-red flesh, and needs a second plum or pluot pollinator nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and plant a compatible plum or pluot pollinator nearby, since Flavor Supreme does not set a reliable crop on its own. Bred by Floyd Zaiger and one of the earliest pluot introductions, Flavor Supreme is still considered by many fruit growers to have the finest flavor of the whole pluot group, with mottled dark red-and-green skin over intensely sweet, richly flavored, deep red flesh that drips juice when fully ripe. It ripens early in the pluot season, and fruit left to color fully on the tree develops noticeably better flavor than fruit picked while still firm and greenish. Thin the heavy early fruit set to improve final size, and manage the tree with the same dormant pruning to an open center used for standard plums.

common_name: Flavor King Pluot (Reddish-Purple Sweet Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; Flavor King is a Zaiger Genetics pluot with reddish-purple skin and deep red, exceptionally sweet flesh, and needs a compatible plum or pluot pollinator such as Santa Rosa nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and provide a compatible pollinator, since Flavor King is not self-fruitful. This Zaiger Genetics pluot ripens to a deep reddish-purple skin over intensely sweet, dark red flesh with very little tartness, making it one of the sweeter pluot selections and a favorite for fresh eating out of hand. It ripens in mid-to-late summer, after earlier pluots like Flavor Supreme have finished, extending the harvest window for gardeners growing more than one pluot variety. As with other pluots, thin heavy fruit sets in late spring to improve final size and quality, and prune in the dormant season to an open center to let light into the canopy.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; Cot-N-Candy is a Zaiger Genetics aprium, an interspecific apricot-plum hybrid weighted mostly toward its apricot parent, with fuzzy orange skin and sweet, aromatic flesh, and needs a compatible pollinator such as an early plum or another aprium/pluot nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and provide a compatible pollinator flowering at the same time, since Cot-N-Candy sets fruit poorly on its own. This Zaiger Genetics aprium, an apricot-plum interspecific hybrid weighted mostly toward apricot, looks much like a fuzzy-skinned apricot but carries noticeably sweeter, richer, more aromatic flesh thanks to its plum parentage. It ripens early in the stone fruit season, giving a jump on the summer harvest, and is generally grown and pruned like a standard apricot, with an open-center form and moderate annual pruning to renew fruiting wood. Because apricots and apriums bloom very early, plant in a site protected from the latest spring frosts, which can damage the flowers before fruit ever sets.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; Flavor Delight is one of the original Zaiger Genetics aprium introductions, ripening very early with sweet, aromatic, apricot-like fruit, and needs a compatible pollinator nearby for good fruit set.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and site it away from the latest spring frost pockets, since aprium flowers open very early and are vulnerable to late cold snaps. Flavor Delight was among the first apriums released by Zaiger Genetics, and it remains valued for ripening earlier than almost any other stone fruit hybrid, giving gardeners a fresh, sweet, apricot-flavored fruit well ahead of the main summer harvest. The reddish-blushed, apricot-like skin covers dense, aromatic, low-acid flesh, and a compatible pollinator, such as an early-flowering plum, pluot, or aprium, is needed nearby since it is not reliably self-fruitful. Prune and thin as for a standard apricot, removing crossing interior branches in the dormant season and thinning heavy fruit sets in spring to improve final size.

common_name: Geo Pride Pluot (Early Red-Skinned Plum-Apricot Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container trees in late winter in well-drained soil in full sun; Geo Pride is a Zaiger Genetics pluot that ripens early in the pluot season with bright red skin and firm, juicy flesh, and needs a compatible plum or pluot pollinator nearby.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and plant a compatible plum or pluot pollinator nearby for good fruit set. Geo Pride is one of the earlier-ripening pluots from Zaiger Genetics, opening the pluot harvest with attractive bright red skin over firm, juicy, sweet-tart flesh that holds up well to picking and handling. Its early season makes it a useful complement to later pluot varieties like Flavor King or Flavor Grenade in a garden with room for more than one, spreading pluot harvest over a longer stretch of summer. Manage the tree as a standard plum, with dormant-season pruning to an open center and spring thinning of heavy fruit sets to improve final size and sweetness.
